title: Asynchronous Programming
introduction: Asynchronous programming allows JavaScript to handle operations that complete later without blocking execution while waiting.

sections.title: async / await
sections.definition: Promise-based syntax for writing asynchronous operations.

questions.title: How do async functions work?
questions.what: An async function always returns a Promise.
questions.how: Execution proceeds synchronously until await suspends the function. Its continuation runs asynchronously when the awaited Promise settles.
questions.why: Makes Promise-based asynchronous control flow easier to express.
questions.when: API requests, asynchronous workflows, and sequential operations.
questions.underTheHood: Promise resolution, fulfillment or rejection, and microtask scheduling coordinate continuation.
questions.interviewAnswer: An async function returns a Promise. Await pauses that function's execution without blocking the JavaScript thread, and its continuation is scheduled asynchronously.
pitfalls: Await does not block the entire JavaScript thread.
followUps: What happens when an awaited Promise rejects?
Does await always introduce an asynchronous continuation?
questions.recall: async F() → Promise → await → suspend F() → settle → microtask → resume

cheatSheet: await → suspend F(), not JS thread
